title: Brother Lawrence in the kitchen
hookLine: a lay brother finds as much of God among the pots as in the chapel (The Practice of the Presence of God)

cards: Picture the sink after a big family dinner. Grease on the pans, somebody's glass with a lipstick mark, the dishwasher already full. It's the least spiritual place in the house.
The deep stuff, it seems, happens somewhere else: on a retreat, on a mountain, in a quiet room with a candle. Dishes are what you get through to get back to real life.
In the sixteen hundreds, in Paris, a clumsy, cheerful lay brother spent fifteen years in a monastery kitchen and came to the opposite conclusion.

teach.h: A SOLDIER, A BARE TREE IN WINTER.
teach.b: His name was Nicolas Herman. He'd been a soldier, wounded in war.
The story he told later is that at eighteen, looking at a bare tree in winter, he realized its leaves would come back in spring, and felt, all at once, how much he was held by God.
Years later he joined the Discalced Carmelites in Paris, not as a priest but as a lay brother, the kind who did the physical work.

teach.h: A LAY BROTHER IN THE KITCHEN.
teach.b: He took the name Brother Lawrence, and they put him in the kitchen. By his own account, he didn't like kitchen work, and wasn't especially good at it. He also found the formal methods of prayer hard.

He decided to do each small thing for the love of God, and to keep talking to God, quietly, all day, as if to a friend in the room. Turning a little omelette in the pan. Picking up a piece of straw from the floor.
After he died, a priest who had talked with him collected his conversations and letters into a small book, The Practice of the Presence of God.

teach.h: WORK TIME, PRAYER TIME: THE SAME.
teach.b: In it, Lawrence says work time was no different for him from prayer time.
In the noise and clatter of his kitchen, with several people calling for different things at once, he felt as close to God as if he were on his knees in chapel.
Catholics treasure the book, and many Protestants and people of other paths read it too. You needn't share his faith to borrow the move. The sink doesn't need to be escaped.

how: Many Christians, Catholic and Protestant, read The Practice of the Presence of God and try to keep a quiet, continual conversation with God through ordinary work, as Brother Lawrence described.

games.q: you're Brother Lawrence. you find formal methods of prayer hard, and you've been sent to the kitchen, which you dislike. what do you do?
o: ask to be moved to the chapel
do each small task for the love of God, talking to God all day

games.why: he does each small thing for the love of God and keeps a quiet conversation going all day. the kitchen becomes as holy to him as the chapel.

practice: If you're near a sink, a counter or a table, wash one cup, wipe one surface or fold one towel; if not, picture it. Do it slowly, and for someone: whoever will use the cup next, the people you share the space with, anyone you love.
If you pray, offer it as Lawrence did, a small thing done with love; if not, just do it completely.

wordCard.voice: Brother Lawrence. The lay brother who found God as near among the pots and the clatter as in the chapel.

carryVoice: Your line: the kitchen is enough. Small things, done with love, count too. Day eighty-seven.
